title: Nicer than he seems
setting: A weekday morning at the office. Mai (Kimura-san at work) is quiet at her desk the day after a meeting with Yamamoto-san, a blunt colleague from another team. Her manager, Tanaka-san, stops by.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, kyou wa genki nai desu ne. kibun demo warui n desu ka?
lines.ja: 木村さん、今日は元気ないですね。気分でも悪いんですか？
lines.kana: きむらさん、きょうはげんきないですね。きぶんでもわるいんですか？
lines.english: Kimura-san, you seem down today. Are you feeling sick or something?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, iie, daijoubu desu. kinou, yamamoto-san to kaigi datta n desu kedo.
lines.ja: あ、いいえ、大丈夫です。昨日、山本さんと会議だったんですけど。
lines.kana: あ、いいえ、だいじょうぶです。きのう、やまもとさんとかいぎだったんですけど。
lines.english: Oh, no, I'm fine. It's just that I had a meeting with Yamamoto-san yesterday.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: aa, yamamoto-san desu ka. nante iwareta n desu ka?
lines.ja: ああ、山本さんですか。何て言われたんですか？
lines.kana: ああ、やまもとさんですか。なんていわれたんですか？
lines.english: Ah, Yamamoto-san. What did he say to you?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: watashi no shigoto o mite, kore, dame desu ne tte. sore dake de, sugu dete itchatta n desu.
lines.ja: 私の仕事を見て、これ、ダメですねって。それだけで、すぐ出て行っちゃったんです。
lines.kana: わたしのしごとをみて、これ、だめですねって。それだけで、すぐでていっちゃったんです。
lines.english: He looked at my work and said, "This won't do." Just that, and then he walked straight out.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sorede, ki ni shiteta n desu ne.
lines.ja: それで、気にしてたんですね。
lines.kana: それで、きにしてたんですね。
lines.english: So that's what's been bothering you.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai. sumimasen, seikaku warui no kana tte, chotto omotchaimashita.
lines.ja: はい。すみません、性格悪いのかなって、ちょっと思っちゃいました。
lines.kana: はい。すみません、せいかくわるいのかなって、ちょっとおもっちゃいました。
lines.english: Yes. I'm sorry, but I did kind of wonder if he's just mean.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: yamamoto-san wa, dare ni demo sou na n desu yo. kanji wa chotto warui desu kedo, seikaku wa ii n desu.
lines.ja: 山本さんは、誰にでもそうなんですよ。感じはちょっと悪いですけど、性格はいいんです。
lines.kana: やまもとさんは、だれにでもそうなんですよ。かんじはちょっとわるいですけど、せいかくはいいんです。
lines.english: Yamamoto-san is like that with everyone. He comes across as a bit unfriendly, but he's a good person.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, sou na n desu ka?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kesa wa, yamamoto-san mo genki nakatta n desu yo.
lines.ja: 今朝は、山本さんも元気なかったんですよ。
lines.kana: けさは、やまもとさんもげんきなかったんですよ。
lines.english: And this morning, Yamamoto-san seemed down too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.kana: え？やまもとさんもですか？

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san ni, kinou wa gomen tte ittoite kudasai, tte. sugoku ki ni shitemashita yo.
lines.ja: 木村さんに、昨日はごめんって言っといてください、って。すごく気にしてましたよ。
lines.kana: きむらさんに、きのうはごめんっていっといてください、って。すごくきにしてましたよ。
lines.english: He asked me to tell you he's sorry about yesterday. It was really bothering him.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou datta n desu ka. shiranakatta desu.
lines.ja: そうだったんですか。知らなかったです。
lines.kana: そうだったんですか。しらなかったです。
lines.english: Oh, I see. I had no idea.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ato, kimura-san wa kanji ga ii shi, shigoto mo dekiru tte, ittemashita yo.
lines.ja: あと、木村さんは感じがいいし、仕事もできるって、言ってましたよ。
lines.kana: あと、きむらさんはかんじがいいし、しごともできるって、いってましたよ。
lines.english: Oh, and he said you're pleasant to work with, and good at your job, too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yamamoto-san, hontou wa seikaku ii n desu ne.
lines.ja: 山本さん、本当は性格いいんですね。
lines.kana: やまもとさん、ほんとうはせいかくいいんですね。
lines.english: So Yamamoto-san is actually a nice person underneath.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. kanji wa ii kedo seikaku ga warui hito mo imasu kara ne.
lines.ja: そうなんです。感じはいいけど性格が悪い人もいますからね。
lines.kana: そうなんです。かんじはいいけどせいかくがわるいひともいますからね。
lines.english: That's right. After all, some people are pleasant on the surface but mean underneath.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou desu ne. yamamoto-san mo genki nai nara, ima kara koe o kakete kimasu.
lines.ja: そうですね。山本さんも元気ないなら、今から声をかけてきます。
lines.kana: そうですね。やまもとさんもげんきないなら、いまからこえをかけてきます。
lines.english: That's true. If Yamamoto-san's feeling down too, I'll go and have a word with him now.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. a, demo, shigoto wa mou ichido mite kudasai ne. yamamoto-san no dame wa, hontou ni dame desu kara.
lines.ja: いいですね。あ、でも、仕事はもう一度見てくださいね。山本さんのダメは、本当にダメですから。
lines.kana: いいですね。あ、でも、しごとはもういちどみてくださいね。やまもとさんのだめは、ほんとうにだめですから。
lines.english: Good idea. Oh, but do look over your work again. When Yamamoto-san says it won't do, it really won't.

choices.english: Tanaka-san warns Mai that Yamamoto-san seems pleasant but is mean underneath.
Mai feels sick after a long meeting, so Tanaka-san tells her to take it easy.
Mai thought Yamamoto-san was mean, but he felt bad about yesterday and had praised her.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-6: after the meeting Yamamoto-san only said 'kore, dame desu ne' (this won't do) and walked out, so Mai wondered if he was mean (seikaku warui no kana). Lines 9-13: Tanaka-san tells her Yamamoto-san was down too, asked him to pass on a 'sorry' (gomen), and said Mai is pleasant to work with and good at her job. In line 16 she decides to go and speak to him. A turns Tanaka-san's point around: he says Yamamoto-san comes across as unfriendly but is a good person (line 7). The people who are pleasant but mean (line 15) are other people, not him. B is wrong: Tanaka-san does ask if she feels sick (kibun demo warui n desu ka?), but in line 2 she says she's fine. She's down (genki nai), not ill.

questions.english: Yuki is about to work with Yamamoto-san for the first time, and she asks you what he's like. Tell her he's a good person underneath, using seikaku.
questions.ja: 山本さんって、どんな人？
questions.kana: やまもとさんって、どんなひと？
questions.answer: Say he's a nice person with seikaku ii (ga drops in casual speech), or seikaku no ii hito before a noun. You can set it against how he comes across, the way Tanaka-san does: kanji wa chotto warui kedo, seikaku wa ii.

modelAnswers.romaji: kanji wa chotto warui kedo, seikaku wa ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 感じはちょっと悪いけど、性格はいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: He comes across a bit unfriendly, but he's a good guy.

modelAnswers.romaji: seikaku no ii hito da yo. hanashite miru to wakaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 性格のいい人だよ。話してみるとわかるよ。
modelAnswers.english: He's a nice person. You'll see once you talk to him.

questions.explanation: Seikaku is who someone is underneath, so seikaku ga ii is the plain way to say someone is a good, kind person. Tanaka-san uses it in line 7 (seikaku wa ii n desu), right after kanji wa chotto warui (he comes across as a bit unfriendly), and Mai says it in line 14 (hontou wa seikaku ii n desu ne). Keep seikaku first: ii seikaku shiteru ne usually sounds sarcastic ('you've got some nerve'). Yuki asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Tanaka-san sees the meeting has been bothering her, what does Mai say she wondered about Yamamoto-san?
questions.ja: 木村さんは、山本さんについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: きむらさんは、やまもとさんについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san wa, yamamoto-san ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: maybe he has a bad personality (word for word)
choices.romaji: warui seikaku o motteru no kana

questions.explanation: Line 6: 'seikaku warui no kana tte, chotto omotchaimashita' (I kind of wondered if he's just mean), with ga dropped as usual. Seikaku ga warui judges what someone is like by nature, so it's a strong thing to say, which is why Mai says sumimasen first. Tanaka-san uses it again in line 15 (seikaku ga warui hito). A is wrong: warui hito judges someone as a bad person in the moral sense, like a crook, and Mai only meant he might be mean. C is a word-for-word calque of 'have a bad personality': Japanese doesn't hold a personality with motsu. Seikaku is the subject and warui describes it.

questions.english: Tanaka-san passes on what Yamamoto-san said about Mai: 'kimura-san wa kanji ga ii shi, shigoto mo dekiru.' What did he mean by kanji ga ii?
questions.ja: 感じがいいって、どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: かんじがいいって、どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: kanji ga ii tte, dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: She's always in a good mood.

questions.explanation: Line 13: kanji (感じ) here is the impression someone's manner gives, so kanji ga ii means she's pleasant to deal with. Tanaka-san sets it against seikaku in line 15 (kanji wa ii kedo seikaku ga warui hito: pleasant on the surface but mean underneath), and in line 7 he says Yamamoto-san himself comes across as a bit unfriendly (kanji wa chotto warui). B mixes it up with kanji (漢字), the Chinese characters, which sound the same; nobody mentions writing. C would be kibun ga ii (in a good mood), which is about how she feels at a given moment, not the impression she makes on people.

questions.english: Your friend Kenta flops onto the sofa with a big sigh and says this. Tell him he seems down and ask what's wrong, using genki.
questions.ja: はあ。今日は何もしたくないなあ。
questions.kana: はあ。きょうはなにもしたくないなあ。
questions.romaji: haa. kyou wa nanimo shitakunai naa.
questions.answer: Say genki nai ne (genki ga nai with ga dropped) to tell him he seems down, then ask dou shita no? Don't say genki ja nai, which leans toward 'unwell', or kibun warui, which means feeling sick.

modelAnswers.romaji: genki nai ne. dou shita no?
modelAnswers.ja: 元気ないね。どうしたの？

modelAnswers.romaji: kenta, kyou zutto genki nai ne. daijoubu?
modelAnswers.ja: ケンタ、今日ずっと元気ないね。大丈夫？
modelAnswers.english: Kenta, you've seemed down all day. You okay?

questions.explanation: Genki ga nai is how someone seems right now: low and flat. Tanaka-san opens with it in line 1 (kyou wa genki nai desu ne), says it about Yamamoto-san in line 9 (genki nakatta), and Mai uses it in line 16 (genki nai nara). Tanaka-san's follow-up in line 1, kibun demo warui n desu ka? (are you feeling sick?), asks about something different, and Mai says she's fine. Kenta is a friend, so casual genki nai ne fits. To Tanaka-san you'd say genki nai desu ne.

newWords.english: person (seikaku no ii hito: a nice person)
